The **staging** half: build → run → predict, plus explicit device placement.

This module takes a compute function (a `@evoxc.defn` forward from
`evoxc_hf.forward_fn`) plus a static config and stages it through the
explicit evoxc pipeline, and it is where the *measured* backend-default matrix
lives (once):

==========================================  ==================================
situation                                   resolution
==========================================  ==================================
`backend` explicit                        used verbatim (explicit > env > default)
`backend=None`, `EVOXC_BACKEND` set       that value is used
`backend=None`, device cpu/None           `"numpy"` (the numpy interpreter)
`backend=None`, device cuda/rocm/vulkan…  `"iree"` (the compiled path)
any compiled backend                        `opt_level="O3"` injected unless passed
`"iree"` + all-ROCm targets               `opt_level="O1"` injected instead
`"iree"` + `["llvm-cpu"]`               `iree_compile_args` injected unless passed
==========================================  ==================================
Every injected default is a *measured* pitfall rather than taste — each one is
documented beside its constant (see `DEFAULT_LLVM_CPU_COMPILE_ARGS`,
`DEFAULT_ROCM_OPT_LEVEL`, and the compile-stage note on
`iree_compile_args`: it must reach `evoxc.compile`, which the one-call
`evoxc.build_cached` composition guarantees, while passing it to `evoxc.lower`
alone is silently ineffective).

Memoisation: the graph is a pure function of `(family, config, seq_len,
batch_size, pack_weights)` — `evoxc_hf.forward_fn` guarantees a stable
object per specialisation — so `build` hands `evoxc.build_cached` a
**stable** `id(fwd)`; that is exactly what makes two identical `build`
calls return the identical `Executable` object instead of recompiling.

**Deliberate deviation from an earlier CONTEXT draft:** the cache key does
**not** include weight identity. Weights are ordinary graph *inputs* (evoxc
principle 6: large tensors are explicit inputs) validated at the run boundary,
so they cannot change the graph; the graph depends only on `(family, config,
seq_len, batch_size, backend, device, options)`. Keying on weights would mean a
pointless recompile per weights object (and per checkpoint load) with zero
change in the compiled program.

Device-resident runs: a non-cpu executable rejects host inputs at the run
boundary by design, so callers must place **both** sides explicitly —
`place_params` for the weights (one `Tensor.to(device)` per leaf) and
`place_ids` for the token ids — and then drive the documented same-device
loop. `run` accepts ids either as a host integer array or as an
`evoxc.Tensor`, and forwards a `Tensor` **verbatim** (no host copy, no
dtype cast, no device move), so a device-resident ids tensor keeps host
round-trips at zero. `predict` is the *host-facing* shorthand and refuses
device params with an error naming that recipe rather than pulling data back to
the host behind the caller's back.

Packed weights (`pack_weights=True`, opt-in): the graph takes a handful of
concatenated params inputs (`evoxc_hf.pack`) instead of one per canonical
weight and unpacks them in-graph with static `evoxc.slice` ops. It exists for one
measured reason — IREE's Python runtime SIGSEGVs above ~161 *consumed* inputs and
the 124M `gpt2` declares 197 — and it changes nothing about the arithmetic:
packing happens once on the host (`evoxc_hf.pack.pack_params`), never per
run. Unpacked stays the default, so no existing caller changes behaviour.

Import-time constraint: only `numpy`, `evoxc` and sibling `evoxc_hf` modules
are imported here. Backend adapters (iree / xla / tvm) are resolved lazily by
`evoxc` itself, so `import evoxc_hf` never imports them.

## Symbols

- [`build`](/api/evoxc-hf/pipeline/build/) — Build (trace → lower → compile → load) the executable of one forward.
- [`place_ids`](/api/evoxc-hf/pipeline/place-ids/) — Copy token ids onto `device` — explicit, one-step placement.
- [`place_params`](/api/evoxc-hf/pipeline/place-params/) — Copy every parameter onto `device` — explicit per-leaf placement.
- [`predict`](/api/evoxc-hf/pipeline/predict/) — Run the whole forward and return host logits — the one host-facing shorthand.
- [`resolve_build_options`](/api/evoxc-hf/pipeline/resolve-build-options/) — Resolve the default backend and the injected compile options.
- [`run`](/api/evoxc-hf/pipeline/run/) — Run a built model executable on one params tree and one id batch.
